alice (support): Saw multiple customer 503s from hosted inference since 06:12 UTC. Customers reporting timeouts and errors. Investigating.
ben (oncall): looking. any correlation with deploy?
alice (support): deploy at 05:58 to inference runtime - but errors start 06:12, steady ramp to 06:25. CPU looks fine, GPU memory trending high.
carol (infra): I see repeated worker exits on upstream hosts. /var/log/infer/runner.log shows SIGABRT and OOM-kill on allocation.
alice (support): paste logs?
carol (infra): ```
[06:12:17] runner: pid=12456 signal=SIGABRT (6) at 0x7f8...
[06:12:17] runtime: Caught OOM while allocating 256MB for KV cache
[06:12:17] python: fatal error: Aborted (core dumped)
```
ben (oncall): that's odd — OOM while allocating KV cache during warmup on shard-7. QPS didn't increase, so looks like a regression in memory accounting.
dave (cs): several paying customers (org-acme, org-beta) hit 503s and saw billing errors. CS is collecting request IDs for refunds.
alice (support): impact: ~8% error rate for hosted endpoints, p95 latency spike from 120ms -> 3-7s.
carol (infra): repro so far: long prompt with model=redwood-v2-16k, context ~12k tokens, concurrency 4 on same worker causes prefetch + KV expansion -> memory surge.
ben (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from affected pool, 2) temporarily cap max_context on runtime to 8k, 3) graceful restart of workers after clearing KV cache.
alice (support): can ops do hot routing? we should fallback to redwood-v2-8k policy.
ben (oncall): on it — initiating traffic-swap for pool eu-west-1-a -> eu-west-1-b fallback now.
devex-bot: :gear: deploybot started rollback of inference-runtime: v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 (change request CR-4821).
carol (infra): attaching quick commands for heap summary & process maps: 
carol (infra): ```sh
# list gpu mem per process
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
# create core dump for analysis (if allowed)
gcore -o /tmp/runner.$(date +%s) 12456 || true
# pmap for resident set
pmap 12456 | tail -n 20
```
ben (oncall): after routing we still observed 1-2 restarts due to SIGABRT during prefetch. Suspect regression in kv-prefetch memory accounting introduced in v2.1.3.
dave (cs): incident banner up, customers notified. CS asked for ETA 1h and will follow up for refunds where needed.
alice (support): assigning to infra for root cause. tagging for postmortem and customer notes.
carol (infra): preliminary suspect: change in v2.1.3 increased initial KV cache growth for long-context models. Rolling back now and will monitor memory churn.
ben (oncall): timeline update: routing started 06:30, errors dropped to <0.5% by 06:38. Keeping watch and will run a controlled repro on a canary host.
alice (support): thanks team. please create incident ticket and include logs, commands, impacted customer list, and repro steps. :white_check_mark:
